name: Chang W. Lee
story_summary: Chang W. Lee is a New York Times photographer with 30 years of experience at the paper, based in Seoul, who joined a scientific expedition aboard the South Korean icebreaker Araon in December 2025 to document the Thwaites Glacier in Antarctica — the world's fastest-thinning glacier, nicknamed the 'Doomsday Glacier.' The expedition carried nearly 40 scientists studying the effects of climate change and potential sea-level rise. Lee packed the Insta360 Ace Pro 2 alongside Sony cameras, DJI drones, and sound-triggered remote cameras to photograph glacier calving. PetaPixel reported on January 8, 2026 that Lee uses the Insta360 specifically to capture 'blind spots' — areas of the ship and ice he physically cannot reach.
why_it_matters: A 30-year New York Times veteran photographer chose the Insta360 Ace Pro 2 as a key tool for one of the most important climate journalism expeditions of 2026 — documenting the Thwaites Glacier, whose complete collapse would raise global sea levels by two feet. The 'blind spots' use case is a compelling, visually concrete demonstration of what Insta360 adds that no other camera can: access to angles a human photographer simply cannot physically reach. Positions Insta360 at the intersection of photojournalism and climate science at the highest professional level.
source_quote: Lee has several smaller cameras, such as the Insta360 Ace Pro 2, which he uses to capture 'blind spots' — areas he physically cannot reach.
